unit.title: Weld using gas metal arc welding process GMAW - (Metal inert gas MIG)

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A WPS for a GMAW job says 'short-circuit transfer'. A welder wants to use spray transfer on a vertical joint to go faster. What should the team leader say?
options: Yes, because faster welding always gives a stronger joint
Yes, as long as the gas flow is doubled to protect the bigger pool
No: spray is for flat and horizontal work; follow the WPS
Yes, if the welder turns the voltage down a little first

questions.stem: Why is short-circuit GMAW often not allowed for thick structural joints?
options: It runs cold and can leave lack of fusion that is hard to see
It makes too much spatter for the steel to be painted afterwards
It uses far more shielding gas than any other transfer mode
It can only be used with pure argon, which costs too much

questions.stem: Why is ER5356 wire often chosen instead of ER4043 for aluminium parts that carry high loads?
options: It melts at a much lower temperature than ER4043 wire
It gives a stronger weld than ER4043
It can be used with carbon dioxide shielding gas
It needs no cleaning of the oxide before welding

questions.stem: Spray and pulsed-spray transfer give a much brighter arc than short-circuit transfer. What should the welder do?
options: Wear clear safety glasses only, as the arc is short
Keep the same lens and look away now and then
Look at the arc through dark sunglasses under the helmet
Choose a darker filter shade to suit the higher current

questions.stem: Four welders run GMAW all day in a production bay. Which fume control should come first?
options: On-torch extraction or a hood at each arc
A paper dust mask for each welder in the bay
Open the doors and rely on the sea breeze
Rotate the welders so each breathes fume for less time

questions.stem: An argon/CO2 cylinder is to be taken to a site job in a van. What is the safe way?
options: Lying loose on the van floor with the regulator still fitted
In the cab with the windows shut so it stays out of the sun
Upright and strapped, regulator off, cap on, van ventilated
With the valve cracked open a little to let pressure out

questions.stem: Spatter from GMAW lands in an open box of rags on a mezzanine floor below. Which control should the team leader have put in place?
options: A bucket of water beside the welder and nothing else
A hot work permit with a cleared area and a fire watch
Welding only in the morning, when the shop is cooler
A sign asking people to keep away from the welding

questions.stem: On a GMAW machine, what does the inductance (arc control) setting change in short-circuit transfer?
options: The speed at which the wire is pulled off the spool by the rolls
The amount of gas that flows out of the nozzle
Which output terminal the gun is connected to
How fast the current rises, which changes spatter and wetting

questions.stem: What is a synergic GMAW machine?
options: One that runs on two shielding gases at the same time
One that can only be used to weld aluminium and stainless steel
One that sets the voltage to suit the wire speed chosen
One with two wire feeders so two welders can use it

questions.stem: What is pulsed GMAW?
options: Current switching between peaks and a low background, for spray at lower heat
Wire fed forward in short bursts each time the welder presses the trigger fast
Gas switched on and off many times a second to save shielding gas
An arc struck and stopped by the welder about once every second

questions.stem: Why is a push-pull gun or spool gun often used to feed soft aluminium wire?
options: Aluminium wire is too heavy for a normal feeder
Soft wire buckles when pushed through a long liner
Aluminium wire must run on DC electrode negative
It keeps the wire warm before it reaches the arc

questions.stem: A machine is changed from steel wire to aluminium wire. Which parts are usually changed?
options: Only the spool, since everything else stays the same
Knurled V-groove rolls and a steel liner for extra grip on the wire
The work clamp and the work lead to an aluminium type
U-groove rolls, a plastic liner and a matching contact tip

questions.stem: A water-cooled GMAW gun is used at high current. What must be checked before welding?
options: That coolant is flowing, or the gun can burn out
That the gun cable is coiled tightly to save space
That the wire is wet so it feeds more smoothly
That the gas is turned off while the coolant runs

questions.stem: Steel with light mill scale or rust must be welded. Which wire is usually better, ER70S-6 or ER70S-3?
options: ER70S-3, because it has more deoxidisers
Either one, because they are the same wire
ER70S-6, because it has more deoxidisers
Neither; scale can only be welded with MMAW

questions.stem: Why is argon with about 2% oxygen or CO2 used for spray transfer on stainless steel, and not pure CO2?
options: Pure CO2 costs far more than argon in Jamaica
Pure CO2 adds carbon and cannot give spray transfer
Pure CO2 is poisonous even in very small amounts
Pure CO2 makes the bead too flat and too wide

questions.stem: What is the main effect of adding more CO2 to an argon/CO2 gas for welding steel?
options: Less penetration and a cleaner, quieter arc
A lower arc voltage with no spatter at all
Spray transfer becomes possible at lower current
Deeper, broader penetration, but more spatter

questions.stem: A cylinder holds about 9 000 litres of gas. The flow is set at 15 L/min. Roughly how many hours of arc-on time will it give?
options: About 10 hours
About 6 hours
About 15 hours
About 60 hours

questions.stem: Wire speed is 8 m/min of 1.0 mm steel wire, which weighs about 6.2 g per metre. About how much wire is used in 30 minutes of arc time?
options: About 15 kg
About 4.8 kg
About 1.5 kg
About 0.15 kg

questions.stem: A 15 kg spool of wire costs J$9 000. A job uses 4 kg. What is the cost of the wire for the job?
Which transfer mode gives large, irregular drops and a lot of spatter, and is usually avoided?
options: Pulsed spray
Short-circuit
Spray
Globular

questions.stem: Why does spray transfer on steel need an argon-rich gas, usually above about 80% argon?
options: With a lot of CO2 the drops cannot leave the wire as a fine spray
Argon is cheaper than CO2, so spray costs much less to run on a job
CO2 would put the arc out at the high currents used
Argon cools the wire so it does not melt too fast

questions.stem: Which transfer mode is best for a vertical-up fillet on 10 mm plate where full fusion is essential?
options: Spray transfer at high current
Globular transfer with CO2
Pulsed spray transfer
Short-circuit at its lowest setting

questions.stem: Why is vertical-down GMAW with short-circuit transfer usually kept for thin sheet only?
options: On thin sheet it always gives far too much penetration
On thicker plate the pool runs ahead and causes cold lap
It needs a special wire that only comes in small sizes
Downhill welding cannot be done with argon mixes

questions.stem: Why is the push (forehand) technique used when GMAW welding aluminium?
options: It gives much deeper penetration than pulling the gun
It lets the welder see the slag forming behind the pool
It stops the wire from touching the contact tip
It gives better gas cover and cleaning ahead of the pool

questions.stem: Why is aluminium cleaned just before welding with a stainless steel brush kept only for aluminium?
options: To remove the oxide without leaving steel particles in the joint
Because a steel brush would make the aluminium magnetic and hard to weld
So the brush can be used to check the root gap as well
To roughen the surface so the wire grips it better

questions.stem: Why is the 4-step (latch) trigger mode useful on long GMAW runs?
options: It doubles the wire speed for the rest of the run after the first click
It switches off the gas part way to save it
The trigger need not be held, and a crater fill can be added
It changes the polarity each time the welder stops

questions.stem: For spray transfer, the contact tip is usually set back inside the nozzle. Why?
options: So the wire can be seen more clearly by the welder
To protect the tip from the higher heat and allow a longer stick-out
So less gas is needed to cover the pool
To stop the wire touching the plate and sticking at the start of each run

questions.stem: A horizontal (2G) butt joint in 8 mm plate is welded with short-circuit GMAW. How is the gun usually angled for the fill runs?
options: Pointed slightly upward to stop the pool sagging
Pointed down towards the lower plate at about 45°
Square to the plate with a long stick-out
Tilted sideways so the wire runs along the top edge

questions.stem: In vertical-up GMAW on a fillet weld, which weave is often used to get good fusion at the toes?
options: A round, circular weave with no pause at all
A fast straight run with no weave of any kind, to keep the heat down
A long whip forward and back along the joint
A triangle or side-to-side weave with a pause at each toe

questions.stem: A GMAW fillet looks smooth, but a break test shows the weld lying on the plate without fusing. What is this, and what usually causes it?
options: Porosity, caused by a dirty or damp wire
Undercut, caused by a wire speed set too high
Cold lap, from low heat or a pool rolling ahead of the arc
Burn-through, caused by a gas flow set much too high for the nozzle

questions.stem: Porosity appears only in the first 20 mm of each GMAW run. Which is the likely cause?
options: The wire speed is set too high for the whole run
Air in the gun lead at the start, or too short a pre-flow
The contact tip is the wrong size for the wire
The welder is pushing instead of pulling the gun

questions.stem: Aluminium GMAW welds show cracks in the crater at the end of each run. Which change helps most?
options: Fill the crater before stopping, using crater fill or a back-step
Stop the run suddenly and lift the gun away fast
Weld the joint with steel wire to strengthen it
Turn off the gas a few seconds before the arc stops so the crater sets

questions.stem: The wire keeps burning back and fusing to the contact tip. Which is a likely cause?
options: The gas flow is set much too high for the job
The nozzle is too long for the work
The plate has been cleaned too well
Wire speed too slow for the voltage, or a worn tip

questions.stem: A short-circuit weld with argon/CO2 has heavy spatter, though the voltage suits the wire speed. What should be checked next?
options: That the gas flow is at least 40 litres per minute
That the wire is ER70S-3 and not ER70S-6
That the polarity is DCEP and the inductance is right
That the plate has been preheated to 200 °C

questions.stem: Which test would best show the fusion inside a GMAW fillet weld on a trial piece?
options: A hardness test on the cap
A macro-etch of a cut section
A spark test on the parent metal
A look with a torch and mirror

questions.stem: A drawing calls for 6 mm fillet welds. A fillet gauge shows legs of 6 mm and 4 mm. What should the inspector record?
options: Accepted, because one of the legs is 6 mm
Accepted, because the average leg is 5 mm
Accepted, as long as the weld looks smooth, even and free of spatter
Undersized: one leg is under 6 mm, so it does not conform

questions.stem: A GMAW procedure test on a butt weld must be checked for porosity inside the weld. Which method is best?
options: Dye penetrant testing
Magnetic particle testing
Radiographic testing
A fillet weld gauge

questions.stem: A long box section is to be GMAW welded along four seams. Which sequence keeps it straightest?
options: Opposite seams in turn, in short balanced lengths
All of one seam first, then the seam next to it
Each seam in one long run, from one end only
The two top seams first, then the two bottom seams

questions.stem: A welder reports that the wire stutters and the arc keeps changing. The contact tip looks fine. What should be checked next?
options: The work clamp's jaws and its spring, then the size of the work lead
The liner for kinks or dirt, and the drive roll tension
The helmet lens for scratches and spatter
The gas cylinder's colour and its label

questions.stem: Why should the gun cable be laid out as straight as possible while welding?
options: So the gas flows faster through the hose
So the cable does not get too hot to touch
So the welding current goes up by a lot
Tight loops add drag in the liner and spoil the feed

questions.stem: You run a trial weld for a new job. Why are the voltage, wire speed, gas flow and travel speed written on the trial record?
options: So the supplier can bill the gas used
So the welder can be paid for the trial time on the next pay sheet
So the settings that passed can be repeated by every welder
So the machine's guarantee stays valid

questions.stem: Two welders on one job are using different gas mixtures because the store ran out of one. What should the team leader do?
options: Stop and check the WPS allows both; if not, get the right gas
Let them carry on, since any argon mix will do for steel
Ask them to share one cylinder by swapping it every hour
Let them finish and note the gas used on the job card

questions.stem: Why is GMAW often a poor choice for welding outdoors on an open site?
options: The machine will not run on site power from a generator
Wind blows away the gas shield, causing porosity
The sun's light makes the arc too hard to see clearly
Outdoor steel is always too thick for GMAW welding

questions.stem: A finished job needs a weld map. What does it show?
options: The route the delivery truck takes to the customer
Where each machine and booth stands in the welding shop, with exits
The price of each weld on the customer's invoice
Each weld's place and number, with welder and inspection result

questions.stem: Galvanised steel has been GMAW welded on a job. What must be done to the weld area afterwards?
options: Nothing, because the zinc flows back over the weld
Wash it down with plain water and leave it to dry
Restore the corrosion protection, such as with zinc-rich paint
Grind off all the zinc for a metre round each weld, then leave it bare

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters FCAW stand for: the wire process often used instead of GMAW outdoors?
What do the letters CTWD stand for: the distance from the end of the contact tip to the work?
In a stainless steel wire grade such as ER308L, what does the letter L mean?
Name the deoxidising element, with the symbol Si, that is added to steel GMAW wire.
What is the name of the small glassy brown or black patches left on a GMAW weld on steel, which must be removed before painting?
A weld must be 1.8 m long. The travel speed is 300 mm per minute. How many minutes of arc time are needed?
A process deposits 2.5 kg of weld metal per hour of arc time. How many hours of arc time are needed to deposit 10 kg?
What is the position code for a fillet weld made in the vertical position?
Name the poisonous gas, with no smell, that forms when the arc breaks down CO2 shielding gas and can build up in a closed space.
What is the name of the spray or gel put on the nozzle and contact tip to stop spatter sticking?
What is the name of the test where the upright plate of a tee joint is hammered over so the fillet weld breaks open to show its inside?
Argon does not react with the weld pool. Which one word describes gases like this?
Which metal is the coating on galvanised steel?
A WPS gives a voltage range of 22–26 V. The welder's meter reads 28 V. By how many volts is it above the top of the range?
What is the name of the device that shows the gas flow in litres per minute, often with a ball in a clear tube?

essays.stem: Compare short-circuit, globular, spray and pulsed-spray transfer in GMAW: how each works, the gas and current each needs, and which positions and thicknesses each suits.
essays.modelAnswer: In short-circuit (dip) transfer the wire touches the pool and shorts many times a second. It uses low current and voltage, works with CO2 or argon/CO2, suits thin sheet and all positions, but can give lack of fusion on thick plate. Globular transfer happens at medium current, mostly with CO2: large drops form and fall unevenly, giving spatter, so it is usually avoided. Spray transfer needs high current and an argon-rich gas. A fine stream of small drops crosses the arc, giving deep fusion and little spatter, but the pool is large and fluid, so it is used flat and for horizontal fillets on thicker plate. Pulsed spray switches between a high peak, which sends one drop, and a low background current. It gives spray-like fusion with less heat, so it can be used in all positions and on thinner metal, including aluminium and stainless.
markingPoints: Short-circuit: wire touches the pool; low heat; thin sheet, all positions; risk of lack of fusion
Globular: large irregular drops, spatter; usually avoided
Spray: high current, argon-rich gas, deep fusion; flat and horizontal on thick plate
Pulsed spray: peak and background current; lower heat; all positions and thinner metal
Links each mode to the right gas and job

essays.stem: Describe how you would set up a GMAW machine and prepare the joint to weld 6 mm aluminium plate, and the technique you would use.
essays.modelAnswer: I would fit a spool gun or push-pull gun, or a short gun with a plastic liner, U-groove drive rolls set to light pressure, and a contact tip for aluminium wire of the right size. The wire would be ER4043 or ER5356, as the WPS says, and the gas pure argon at the flow the WPS gives. Polarity is DCEP. The joint is degreased with a clean solvent, then the oxide is brushed off with a stainless brush kept only for aluminium, just before welding. Thick joints may get a small bevel. Aluminium draws heat away quickly, so I would use spray or pulsed transfer with enough current to wet in at the start. I would push the gun at about 10–15°, travel fairly fast with a steady speed, and fill the crater at the end of each run to stop crater cracks.
markingPoints: Spool or push-pull gun (or plastic liner), U-groove rolls, aluminium tip
Correct wire (ER4043/ER5356), pure argon, DCEP, settings from the WPS
Degreases, then removes oxide with a dedicated stainless brush just before welding
Spray or pulsed transfer; push technique with steady, fairly fast travel
Fills the crater to avoid crater cracks

essays.stem: As team leader, describe how you would develop and record the settings for a new GMAW job with 8 mm fillet welds on 10 mm steel, from a trial piece to approved settings.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start with the drawing and the WPS, or the wire maker's data if there is no WPS yet, to choose the wire size, gas, transfer mode and a starting voltage and wire speed. I would make a trial tee joint from the same steel, in the same position as the job. After welding I check the leg sizes with a fillet gauge, look at the shape and the toes, and then cut and etch or break the joint to see the fusion at the root. If the fusion or size is wrong I change one setting at a time and try again. When the trial passes, I write down the wire, gas and flow, voltage, wire speed, stick-out, gun angles, travel speed and position, and get the supervisor to approve them. The approved settings are posted at the welding station so every welder uses them.
markingPoints: Uses the drawing and WPS or maker's data to choose starting settings
Makes a trial joint in the same material and position as the job
Checks size with a gauge and fusion by cutting, etching or breaking
Changes one setting at a time until the trial passes
Records all settings, gets approval and shares them with the welders

essays.stem: Explain why lack of fusion is a special risk in short-circuit GMAW, how it can be found, and how you would prevent it on a production job.
essays.modelAnswer: Short-circuit transfer uses low heat, and the weld can look smooth and neat even when the metal has not melted into the plate or the run below. This cold lap is hidden inside the joint, so a visual check alone may pass a weak weld. It is more likely on thick plate, with a large pool rolling ahead of the arc, with travel that is too slow or too fast, or with voltage too low. It can be found by breaking or cutting and etching test pieces, and on the job by ultrasonic testing. To prevent it I would follow a WPS that suits the thickness, use spray or pulsed spray on thicker joints, keep the arc at the front of the pool, use the right gun angles and steady travel, and make sure welders are trained and qualified. I would also break-test sample pieces during production.
markingPoints: Low heat; weld can look good but not be fused (hidden cold lap)
Causes: thick plate, pool rolling ahead, wrong travel or low voltage
Found by break tests, cut and etch, or ultrasonic testing
Prevented by the right WPS, transfer mode, arc at the front of the pool, angles and steady travel
Trained, qualified welders and sample testing during production

essays.stem: Explain how the choice of shielding gas affects GMAW welds on carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminium. Give the usual gas for each and the reason.
essays.modelAnswer: For carbon steel, pure CO2 is cheap and gives deep penetration, but it gives more spatter and cannot give spray transfer. Argon mixed with about 5–25% CO2 gives a smoother arc, less spatter and a better bead, and the mixes with less CO2 allow spray transfer. For stainless steel, argon with a small amount of CO2 or oxygen (about 2%) is used, so the arc is steady but little carbon is added, which would harm the corrosion resistance. Special three-part mixes are also used for short-circuit work on stainless. For aluminium, pure argon is used, or argon with helium for thick sections to give more heat. Oxygen and CO2 are never used on aluminium because they oxidise the pool. In every case the gas must keep air away from the pool, so the flow and draughts must be controlled.
markingPoints: Carbon steel: CO2 for penetration but spatter; argon/CO2 for smoother arc and spray
Stainless: argon with about 2% CO2 or oxygen, or a special mix; keeps carbon low
Aluminium: pure argon, or argon/helium for thick work; no oxygen or CO2
Explains that the gas protects the pool from air
Mentions flow and draught control

essays.stem: Describe how you would GMAW weld stainless steel sheet for a food-processing table so that the finished weld keeps its corrosion resistance.
essays.modelAnswer: I would use the stainless wire the WPS gives, such as ER308LSi for 304 sheet, with the argon mix made for stainless. The work area and tools must be kept apart from carbon steel: stainless-only brushes, grinding discs and clamps, and benches covered so carbon steel dust does not touch the sheet. The joint is cleaned with a suitable solvent and a stainless brush. Stainless holds heat and distorts easily, so I would use pulsed or short-circuit transfer with low heat, tack closely, and weld in short lengths with cooling between them. Too much heat leaves dark heat tint and lowers corrosion resistance. Where the back of the weld is on a food surface, a back purge or backing gas may be needed. After welding, the weld is blended smooth and the heat tint removed by the cleaning method the Centre allows, so the surface is clean and easy to sanitise.
markingPoints: Correct stainless wire and gas from the WPS
Keeps stainless apart from carbon steel: separate tools, brushes and discs
Low heat: pulsed or short-circuit, close tacks, short runs and cooling
Back purge or backing gas where the back face matters
Removes heat tint and blends the weld for a smooth, cleanable finish

essays.stem: A welder reports porosity, an unsteady arc and poor wire feed on the same machine. Describe, step by step, how you would find and fix the cause.
essays.modelAnswer: First I make the machine safe and look at the simple things. I check the cylinder is not empty, the gas flow is correct at the flowmeter, and there are no leaks in the hose or fittings, using leak-test fluid. I check for draughts from fans or doors. Then I look at the gun: spatter in the nozzle, a loose or worn contact tip, the wrong tip size, and a damaged gas diffuser. Next I check the wire path: the spool brake, the drive roll size and pressure, and the liner for kinks, dirt or wear, blowing it out or replacing it. I check the work clamp is tight on clean metal and the cables are not damaged. I also check the wire and plate are clean and dry. I change one thing at a time and test on scrap, then record the fault and the fix in the maintenance log.
markingPoints: Checks gas: cylinder contents, flow, leaks and draughts
Checks gun parts: nozzle, contact tip, diffuser
Checks feed: spool brake, drive rolls, liner
Checks the work clamp, cables and cleanliness of wire and plate
Changes one thing at a time, tests and records the fix

essays.stem: Explain the health and safety hazards in a GMAW production bay with four welders, and the controls you would put in place as team leader, using the hierarchy of controls.
essays.modelAnswer: The main hazards are welding fume and gases, arc radiation, electric shock, burns and fire from spatter, noise from grinding, cylinders falling, and heat stress in a hot Jamaican workshop. Using the hierarchy of controls, I would first remove or reduce the hazard where I can, for example by buying steel without paint or galvanising, or choosing lower-fume settings. Next come engineering controls: on-torch extraction or hoods at each bay, screens between bays, cylinders chained upright, and good general ventilation. Then administrative controls: a hot work procedure, a fire watch where needed, training, work rotation and rest and water breaks in the heat. Last is PPE: helmets with the right shade, flame-resistant clothing, gloves, boots, hearing protection, and respirators where fume is still high. I would check these controls daily and record any problems.
markingPoints: Lists the main hazards: fume, radiation, shock, fire, noise, cylinders, heat
Elimination or substitution first
Engineering controls: extraction, screens, secured cylinders, ventilation
Administrative controls: procedures, training, fire watch, breaks
PPE last, with daily checks by the team leader

essays.stem: Describe how you would GMAW weld a vertical-up (3G) single-V butt joint in 10 mm steel plate. Include the transfer mode, settings, gun angles and weave.
essays.modelAnswer: I would follow the WPS, which for vertical-up on 10 mm plate would usually call for short-circuit transfer with care, or pulsed spray if the machine has it. The plates are bevelled, cleaned to bright metal, gapped and tacked. The settings are set lower than for flat welding, and checked on a scrap piece in the same position. For the root I point the gun slightly upward, about 5–10° from square, with a steady stick-out, and use a small side-to-side movement to keep a keyhole and fuse both root faces. For the fill and cap I use a side-to-side or triangle weave, moving quickly across the middle and pausing at each edge so the sides fuse and there is no undercut. I keep the arc at the front of the pool so it does not roll over cold metal. Each run is cleaned and checked before the next.
markingPoints: Follows the WPS: short-circuit or pulsed spray, lower settings tested on scrap
Prepares, cleans, gaps and tacks the joint
Gun pointed slightly upward with steady stick-out
Weave with a pause at the edges; arc kept at the front of the pool
Cleans and checks each run

essays.stem: A job has 20 m of 6 mm fillet weld. Each metre needs about 0.2 kg of wire and 4 minutes of arc time. Wire costs J$700 per kg and gas flows at 15 L/min. Work out the wire used, the wire cost and the gas used, and explain what else a real estimate should include.
essays.modelAnswer: Wire used: 20 m × 0.2 kg = 4 kg. Wire cost: 4 kg × J$700 = J$2 800. Arc time: 20 m × 4 minutes = 80 minutes. Gas used: 80 minutes × 15 L/min = 1 200 litres. The gas cost is found from the price of a cylinder and how many litres it holds. A real estimate must also include the gas used for purging and between welds, wire lost as offcuts and spatter, labour for fit-up, tacking, welding, cleaning and inspection (which takes much longer than the arc time), contact tips, nozzles and grinding discs, power, machine costs, and any testing. A contingency should be added for problems, and GCT shown separately at the current rate.
markingPoints: Wire used: 4 kg
Wire cost: J$2 800
Arc time 80 minutes; gas used 1 200 litres
Adds labour, consumables, waste and gas lost, power and testing
Adds contingency and shows GCT separately at the current rate

practical1.title: Set the GMAW parameters, then weld vertical-up (3F) and overhead (4F) fillets on 10 mm steel, with break tests and a weld record
practical1.brief: As a group, read the job sheet and procedure the assessor gives you. Make a trial tee joint on 10 mm steel in the vertical-up position, check it, and agree the settings (voltage, wire speed, gas flow and stick-out) before production welding. Record the trial and the agreed settings. Each member then welds two tee joints, one vertical-up (3F) and one overhead (4F), to the agreed settings, while another member acts as inspector and records the settings used. When cool, the group checks every weld with a fillet gauge and records the results. The assessor breaks one joint from each member (fillet break test) and the group records what the break shows. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the trial and weld records to the group's practical.
materials: Strips of 10 mm carbon steel, about 150 mm × 50 mm, for tee joints (two joints per member, plus trial pieces)
GMAW machines with ER70S-6 wire (1.0 mm or 1.2 mm) and argon/CO2 gas
Positioners or stands for vertical and overhead work
Fillet weld gauges, a steel rule and a square
Grinder, wire brush, nozzle pliers and anti-spatter
Trial record and weld record sheets
photos: The trial joint, and the trial record with the agreed settings
A tee joint tacked and fixed in the vertical-up position
A member welding overhead in full PPE
A fillet gauge on a finished weld
The broken fillet showing the fusion
The completed weld record and the cleaned area
checklist: Took part in setting and recording the trial settings
Checked the gas, wire feed and gun parts before welding
Wore full PPE, with head cover for overhead work
Kept to the agreed settings and correct gun angles in both positions
Finished fillets to size, with equal legs and no undercut or porosity
Break test showed fusion at the root and both plates
Recorded settings and gauge results accurately as inspector
Shut down the gas and left the area clean and safe
safety: Cylinders chained upright; leak-test fittings before use
Weld in screened bays; warn others before striking an arc
Use extraction at the arc and keep your head out of the fume
Wear a cap, collar and sleeves when welding overhead
Treat welded pieces as hot; use tongs and mark them HOT
Only the assessor breaks the test pieces; stand clear and wear eye protection

practical2.title: Change a GMAW set over to aluminium, then weld and inspect butt and fillet joints in 4–6 mm aluminium
practical2.brief: As a group, plan and carry out the change-over of a GMAW set from steel to aluminium: fit a spool gun or push-pull gun, or a plastic liner, U-groove rolls and the right contact tip, load aluminium wire and connect pure argon. Record each step on a change-over checklist. Each member then cleans and welds one butt joint and one tee (fillet) joint in 4 mm to 6 mm aluminium plate in the flat or horizontal position, using the push technique and filling the crater at the end. A second member watches and records the settings. The group inspects every weld by eye and with a gauge and records the results. At the end, the group changes the set back to steel (or as the assessor directs) and records that too. Photograph each stage and add the photos and records to the group's practical.
materials: GMAW machine with a spool gun or push-pull gun (or a plastic liner and U-groove rolls)
ER4043 or ER5356 aluminium wire, and aluminium contact tips
Aluminium plate 4–6 mm, about 150 mm × 75 mm (two butt pieces and two tee pieces per member)
Stainless steel brushes kept for aluminium, and a clean solvent with rags
Fillet gauge, steel rule and the change-over checklist and weld record
photos: The parts changed: rolls, liner or gun, and tip
The aluminium wire loaded and the argon connected
A member cleaning a joint with the aluminium-only brush
A member welding with the push technique, in full PPE
Each member's finished butt and fillet welds
A filled crater at the end of a run
The completed change-over checklist and weld record
checklist: Helped change the set over correctly and recorded it
Cleaned the joint with solvent and an aluminium-only brush just before welding
Used the push technique with a steady speed and correct angles
Filled the crater at the end of each run
Welds even, fused at both edges, with no cracks or heavy porosity
Recorded settings and inspection results accurately
Kept solvent and rags away from the arc and stored them safely afterwards
safety: Keep solvents closed and away from the arc; let wiped surfaces dry before welding
Use extraction: aluminium welding makes ozone and fume
Wear a darker filter shade for the bright spray arc
Cylinders chained upright; close the cylinder valve when not in use
Switch the machine off before changing rolls, liner or tips
